items.explanation: The canonical text prints Umar, although the immediately preceding chain names Amr ibn Dinar and contains no Umar. None of the supplied witnesses contains this passage. The translation therefore retains Umar rather than silently emending it to Amr, and the names array treats the two printed forms separately.

items.arabic_span: البخاري ومسلم ويروى عن معمر عن الزهري
items.explanation: “Al-Bukhari and Muslim” appears without a governing verb or decisive punctuation, and the supplied witnesses do not clarify its relationship to the surrounding statements. items.arabic_span: وأبو نعيم في طريقه، ومن طريق إسحاق بن عبد اللَّه
items.explanation: The canonical reading literally gives “Abu Nu'aym in his line of transmission,” whereas manuscript A reads “through his line of transmission.” The supplied collateral witnesses do not establish the intended construction or the exact attachment of the following Ishaq chain. items.arabic_span: بن أمية بن محرث بن حمل بن شق بن رقبة بن مخدج

items.arabic_span: ورواه النّاس بن مالك، عن شيخه الزّهريّ

items.arabic_span: زينب بن ثعلبة / زينب بنت ثعلبة

items.arabic_span: دعتني أم كليبة بنت برثن العنبرية

items.arabic_span: عزمت عليك إلا تثبت، حتى تسود يداك من الخضاب

items.arabic_span: عن عبد العزيز بن عبد اللَّه بن عامر بن ربيعة، عن أمه ليلى

items.arabic_span: تنبت أجسادنا على أرواح أهل الجنة

items.explanation: The transmitted wording is geographically and grammatically unstable. The Urdu witness does not establish the intended localities, and the supplied collateral Arabic entries omit this sentence; therefore Hafar and al-Safa remain provisional readings.

items.arabic_span: التي اختلعت من زوجها وتزوّجها خولة أمّها معاذة

items.arabic_span: بنت عبد اللَّه بن أبي مالك ... وأبوها هو عبد اللَّه بن أبي ابن سلول

items.arabic_span: عن عمرو بن شعيب، هو أخو عمرو، عن أبيه، عن جدّه
items.explanation: The words «هو أخو عمرو» are present in the canonical Arabic and corroborated by the Urdu translation witness, but their pronoun referent and the identity of 'Amr are incoherent in this isnad. No supplied independent Arabic witness provides a defensible emendation. The final text therefore retains the words literally without resolving or silently altering them.

The isnad names this transmitter only as Abd Allah. The supplied witnesses do not establish whether he is Abd Allah ibn Unays or someone else, so the translation preserves the bare name without expansion.

items.arabic_span: فقال عمر لنعيم: خطب إليك ابن أخيك فرددته
items.explanation: The canonical wording explicitly says “your nephew,” but this conflicts with the fuller narrative, in which Abdullah ibn Umar is the suitor and Nuaym’s orphaned nephew is a different prospective match. The collateral account and supplied Urdu pages do not establish which nephew the abridged wording intends, so the literal reference has been preserved without identifying him.

The canonical edition prints بلفظة. The probable contextual sense is “with that wording,” but it may be a typographical form of بلفظه. The Urdu witness abbreviates the citation and therefore cannot decide the reading.

The canonical text unmistakably says “the killing of Uthman ibn Mazun,” which the translation preserves. The collateral Arabic report describes illness and death, while the Urdu witness has “martyrdom”; without another al-Isabah manuscript, it cannot be determined whether قتل is authorial or a textual corruption.

items.arabic_span: طاولنا عثمان بن مظعون السكنى لما افترقت الأنصار
items.explanation: The canonical construction is anomalous. The collateral Usd al-Ghaba account instead says that Uthman fell to their lot when the Ansar drew lots, but that wording cannot replace the authoritative al-Isabah text. The translation therefore retains the apparent senses “vied” and “separated.”
The supplied witnesses do not establish the precise vocalization. “Umm Subay'” is retained provisionally because no evidence supports a safer replacement.

The consonantal spelling is confirmed, but neither the canonical Arabic nor the Urdu witness supplies vowels sufficient to establish the exact vocalization. The candidate form Ja'una is therefore retained provisionally.

items.arabic_span: وقال ابن سعد: أخرج حديثها أبو داود، والترمذي
items.explanation: The printed attribution to Ibn Sa'd is chronologically anomalous because the dates supplied in footnote 2 place his death before those of Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi. No supplied witness establishes a different reading, so the canonical wording has been translated without silent emendation.
The text specifies that the zay is vowelless but does not mark the vowel of the initial fa. “Umm Fazr” is retained provisionally because the supplied witnesses do not establish the vocalization.
This may be a printing error for another bibliographical title, but no supplied evidence authorizes an emendation. It is therefore retained diplomatically as “Tahdhib al-Kalam.”
The consonantal form is secure, but neither the canonical text nor the supplied witnesses establish its precise vocalization. “Qartha'” is therefore a provisional consonantal transliteration.

The source fixes the medial undotted ha as quiescent and followed by lam but does not explicitly state the initial kaf's vowel. “Umm Kuhla” is used provisionally in the final text, but “Umm Kahla” cannot be excluded securely from the supplied evidence.

The canonical text clearly prints 3/4510, and that reading has therefore been preserved. The supplied witnesses do not establish whether this unusual Musnad Ahmad locator is itself a typographical error.

The printed canonical Arabic contains al-dar immediately before al-Daraqutni. The supplied Urdu and collateral witnesses do not contain the sentence, so it cannot be determined whether this is a simple typographical duplication or another corruption. The English therefore identifies al-Daraqutni while explicitly recording the printed wording.
The witnesses confirm the narrator's identity and the consonantal spelling, but do not establish the precise vocalization. “Samawayh” is therefore retained provisionally.

items.arabic_span: بايعنا رسول اللَّه وأن رسول اللَّه دعا له ومسح صدره
items.explanation: The evidence establishes that these words are not part of al-Haythami's quoted evaluation, but it does not establish where the two appended report fragments originally belonged. They are therefore preserved without a new attribution.

items.arabic_span: من يتهم يا رسول اللَّه، فإنّي لا أتهم بأبي إلا الشاة المسمومة التي أكل معك
items.explanation: The canonical page reads “Who is suspected?” and “my father,” while the cited Abu Dawud report reportedly reads “What is thought to be the cause of your illness?” and “my son,” and additionally mentions Khaybar. Because the canonical Arabic was designated authoritative and facts absent from it may not be introduced, the final translation retains its printed wording conservatively.
The printed order 78/3 has been preserved. The supplied evidence cannot determine whether the intended reference was instead 3/78.
The source supplies page 201 but no volume number; the available evidence does not establish the omitted volume or edition.

items.arabic_span: أنها أتت أم معبد بنت الأشعر
items.explanation: The feminine subject of “she came” is implicit. Neither the canonical wording nor the supplied witnesses securely identifies her, so the translation preserves the pronoun without assigning an identity.
The note unambiguously reads “Umm Mu'attib,” which has been preserved. The supplied witnesses do not establish whether it represents a variant heading, a correction, or a separate cross-reference.

items.arabic_span: وابن أبي فديك من أقرانه، فلعله حمله عنه، ولم يفصح باسم ابنه لصغره. قال محمد بن إسحاق: فالتبس
items.explanation: The supplied evidence does not securely determine every referent of “his,” “him,” and “his son,” whose youth is intended, or the precise syntactic connection of “Muhammad ibn Ishaq said.” The English therefore preserves the source's pronoun sequence without silently reassigning it.

The authoritative Arabic literally reads “her mother.” Collateral accounts suggest that Umm Mani' herself may be intended and that أمها could be corrupt, but those works are not manuscript witnesses to al-Isabah and cannot establish an emendation. The final translation therefore preserves the canonical wording literally.

The phrase literally says that the transmission was heard “in the fifth,” but neither the canonical wording nor the supplied witnesses identifies whether this denotes a year of age, a calendar year, or another chronological reference.

items.arabic_span: إلى أن غرفت في السبيل في خلافة عمر
items.explanation: The supplied witnesses do not verify this anomalous wording. The final text therefore uses the contextual rendering “swept away by a flood” and does not adopt “drowned.” Searchable reproductions outside the supplied witness set instead read غرقت في السيل, including an [al-Isabah facsimile](https://www.cia.gov/library/abbottabad-compound/AE/AED120ADBAEA1006F669D935962EA163_VOL8.pdf) and an [independent textual reproduction](https://sahaba.rasoolona.com/Sahaby/26956/%D8%AA%D9%81%D8%B5%D9%8A%D9%84-%D9%85%D8%A7-%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%B1-%D8%B9%D9%86%D9%87%D8%A7-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%83%D8%AA%D8%A8-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%B1%D8%A8%D8%B9%D8%A9/%D8%A3%D9%85-%D9%86%D9%87%D8%B4%D9%84-%D8%A8%D9%86%D8%AA-%D8%B9%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D9%86-%D8%B3%D8%B9%D9%8A%D8%AF-%D8%A8%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%B5-%D8%A8%D9%86-%D8%A3%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%A9), but the authoritative supplied Arabic cannot be silently replaced on that basis.
Neither the Arabic nor the supplied Urdu witness identifies the antecedent of “from him.” The final translation deliberately preserves that ambiguity.

items.arabic_span: عن الحسن بن موسى [عن] الأشعث عنه
items.explanation: The matching collateral chains support taking “عنه” as referring to Ibn Lahi'a, but they omit al-Ash'ath and therefore do not resolve his identity, exact position, or the status of the bracketed preposition beyond the canonical editorial note. The final translation preserves the canonical sequence.

The supplied evidence does not identify this al-Hasan or establish any rearrangement of the route. The final translation therefore retains the canonical wording without merging him with al-Hasan ibn Musa.

The canonical Arabic and Urdu witness both read “Muslim and his father,” so that wording is retained. Muslim does not occur in the preceding isnad, however, and the evidence cannot determine whether the name is an authorial or scribal error for Sulaym.

The note clearly pertains to the Umm Hisham report, but no [4] callout appears in the supplied Arabic body and the evidence does not establish its original position. The note is therefore retained without an invented callout.

The phrase is grammatically incomplete and ends with an explicit ellipsis. No supplied witness contains the colophon, so the missing relationship among “we,” “him,” and “whoever looks into it” cannot be recovered safely. The English preserves the fragment literally.

The construction is awkward, and the witnesses do not establish whether بالتحقيق is adverbial or reflects a textual disturbance. “Upon verification” is the most conservative contextual rendering, but the precise construction remains uncertain.

items.arabic_span: وقد بقي عليه المبهمات، وقيد كثيرا منهما، والكنى لم أظفر به إلى الآن
items.explanation: The referents of the dual منهما are not supplied, while the following plural الكنى is resumed by singular به. No relevant witness resolves the wording. The translation therefore retains “the two of them” and the singular “it.”
The unvocalized spelling supports the mechanical form al-Wandi, but the supplied evidence does not establish its historical pronunciation or identification.
Hadir is a reasonable mechanical transliteration, but the unvocalized Arabic and unrelated witnesses do not establish the precise pronunciation.
Al-Damhawhi mechanically represents the canonical consonantal spelling, but its precise vocalization and identification cannot be established from the supplied evidence.
